message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a compiled binary by BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATION ONLY.

Binary: /workspace/executable  (a spaced-repetition CLI called "hashcards", version 0.3.0)
Docs: /workspace/README.md ; example collection: /tmp/explore/_example_master (copy it, never modify the master)

HARD RULES (violating these fails the whole task):
- NEVER decompile, disassemble, or inspect the binary bytes (no objdump, nm, strings, readelf, ghidra, gdb, hexdump on /workspace/executable).
- NEVER use strace/ltrace/perf or any tracing on /workspace/executable.
- NEVER search the internet or any package registry for the project source code. You have no network anyway.
- ONLY run the binary with CLI args / HTTP requests and observe stdout, stderr, exit codes, files it writes, and HTTP responses.

Environment: python3 (3.10, has sqlite3 module), curl, no network. Use python3 to inspect the hashcards.db SQLite file.

Working discipline:
- Work ONLY inside your own scratch dir (mkdir -p it).
- Write detailed findings to your findings file as you go. Be exhaustive and BYTE-EXACT: paste literal expected output, exact error strings, exact exit codes.
- Save large artifacts (full HTML/CSS/JS/JSON dumps) as separate files in a sibling directory and reference them.
- Your final returned text must be a dense, complete summary of the RULES you inferred (not a narration of what you tried). Someone must be able to reimplement from it.
- Prefer many small experiments. Test edge cases aggressively. When you see a rule, try to break it.

AREA: Markdown to HTML rendering used by the drill web UI. Use --port 8305 --open-browser false over a scratch collection you control; change the markdown, restart, re-fetch.

Determine the exact HTML produced for:
- paragraphs, soft/hard line breaks, headings, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline code, fenced code blocks with and without a language (is a highlight.js class emitted?), blockquotes, ordered/unordered/nested lists, tables (GFM?), task lists, footnotes, autolinks, raw inline HTML, horizontal rules, entity escaping, smart punctuation (are quotes/dashes/ellipses transformed?).
- math: inline single-dollar and display double-dollar - what HTML does the server emit (raw text left for client-side KaTeX, or server-side rendered)? Read /script.js to see how the client renders math and which delimiters it configures.
- The macros.tex file in the collection root: figure out its format (the example contains a line defining a macro named euler) and how macros reach the client (embedded in the HTML? passed to KaTeX?). Test multiple macros, macros with arguments, comments, blank lines.
- images: relative src, the @/ prefix form, remote URLs, missing files. What src does the emitted img tag have? How is the media file served over HTTP?
- audio/video: an image-syntax link to an .mp3 - is it turned into an audio element? Which extensions map to audio/video? Exact HTML.
- cloze cards: how is the deleted span rendered on the question side vs the answer side (span/class)? Capture both.
- The card HTML skeleton and the answer-side variant.
Save byte-exact samples and write out the rules.

Your scratch dir is /tmp/explore/drill-render. Write findings to /tmp/findings/drill-render.md and artifacts under /tmp/findings/drill-render/.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Hashcards

A plain text-based spaced repetition system.

Features:
- Store flashcards as plain Markdown files (front/back and cloze cards supported).
- Content-addressable cards: cards are identified by the hash of their text.
- Low friction: edit cards with your editor of choice; use standard tools and VCS.
- Efficient scheduling using an established spaced-repetition algorithm.

Example deck (a Markdown file):

```
Q: How many neurons are there in the human brain?
A: ~80 billion.

C: An [agonist] is a ligand that binds to a receptor and [activates it].
```

Installation

Download a pre-built binary from the project's releases page: https://github.com/eudoxia0/hashcards/releases

Usage

Start a drilling session for a directory containing your Markdown decks:

```
$ hashcards drill [DIRECTORY]
```

Common commands

- drill [DIRECTORY]      Start a drilling session (launches a local web interface).
- stats [DIRECTORY]      Print collection statistics (JSON output supported).
- check [DIRECTORY]      Check integrity of a collection.
- orphans list|delete    Manage orphan cards in a collection.
- export [DIRECTORY]     Export a collection to JSON (prints to stdout by default).

Configuration & data

Runtime data (such as review progress) is stored in a collection database (e.g. an SQLite file) in the root of your card collection directory. This README intentionally omits implementation-specific details (internal schemas, build instructions, and developer notes).

For detailed user-oriented documentation and examples, see the example/ directory (if present) in this repository.

This project is distributed under the terms of the LICENSE file included in this repository.

Commands:
  drill    Drill cards through a web interface
  check    Check the integrity of a collection

  orphans  Commands relating to orphan cards

Drill cards through a web interface

Usage: executable drill [OPTIONS] [DIRECTORY]

Arguments:
  [DIRECTORY]
          Path to the collection directory. By default, the current working directory is used

Options:
      --card-limit <CARD_LIMIT>
          Maximum number of cards to drill in a session. By default, all cards due today are drilled

      --new-card-limit <NEW_CARD_LIMIT>
          Maximum number of new cards to drill in a session

      --host <HOST>
          The host address to bind to. Default is 127.0.0.1
          
          [default: 127.0.0.1]

      --port <PORT>
          The port to use for the web server. Default is 8000
          
          [default: 8000]

      --from-deck <FROM_DECK>

      --open-browser <OPEN_BROWSER>
          Whether to open the browser automatically. Default is true

      --answer-controls <ANSWER_CONTROLS>
          Which answer controls to show:

          Possible values:
          - full:   Show all four rating buttons (Forgot/Hard/Good/Easy)
          - binary: Show only two rating buttons (Forgot/Good)
          
          [default: full]

      --bury-siblings <BURY_SIBLINGS>
